title: Sorting with Interfaces
story: You have a list of scores, names, and dates - all need sorting. But sorting logic differs: numbers by value, strings alphabetically, dates chronologically. An interface captures 'can be compared' so you write sort ONCE.
why: The Comparable interface lets you write a single sort function that works for any type that can be ordered, through bubble sort or any algorithm.
analogy: A librarian can sort books by title, author, or year because books provide comparable properties. The librarian's sorting method doesn't change - only what property they compare. The Comparable interface is the 'comparable property' contract.
try_it: Implement Comparable for a `Name` type (wrapper around Str) and sort alphabetically. Then create `TimedScore` that compares by time (smaller = better). Run each through the same sort function.
tips: `&Self` in an interface method means 'reference to the same type'
Bubble sort works by repeatedly comparing adjacent elements and swapping
The sort function only needs is_greater - equality is for stable sorts
common_mistakes: Comparing wrong fields - make sure is_greater compares what you intend to sort by
Forgetting to use `&mut` on the Vec parameter - sorting modifies in place
Swapping without clone() - you need copies of the values to swap
